issues.competing_evidence: Shafter+83 scanned Table VI defines q=M2/M1=0.71 +/-0.10 and gives M1=0.99 +/-0.15, M2=0.70 +/-0.03 Msun, i=57 +/-11. Coppejans+16 q=1.4 +/-0.2 is the reciprocal convention. Saitou+12 gives M2 uncertainty +/-0.15 and i=68 from Hartley; Harrison+18/RKCat reports M1=1.00 +/-0.06 and M2=0.77 +/-0.03; Boneva+24 reports M2=0.70 +/-0.02.
issues.why_it_matters: Component masses and q convention affect population comparisons and any Roche geometry; compilations conflict in uncertainties and inclination interpretation.
issues.needed_action: Choose which mass branch, if any, the community-facing summary should display; retain all ledger rows and conventions until the source-chain differences are resolved.

issues.competing_evidence: Wade+81 full thesis gives minimum-light K5-or-later, most likely K7; Harrison+18 JHK spectrum/equivalent-width/model analysis favors early-M/M1.3-M1.6 but notes contamination and adopts T2=3575 K as a light-curve input. Boneva+24 repeats the Harrison result.
issues.why_it_matters: Donor type, temperature and Roche-radius interpretation affect evolutionary and CMD comparisons; the estimates use different wavelength regions and model assumptions.
issues.needed_action: Decide whether the public display should show both historical optical K7 and later infrared early-M interpretations, or select one only after reviewing the original donor spectra/contamination assumptions.

issues.competing_evidence: Hartley+05 abstract favors a uniform metal-enriched 57,000 K WD model; an alternative 29% at 72,000 K plus 71% at 26,000 K fits slightly better but was not required. Harrison+18 uses 26,000 K as a WISE light-curve model input. Boneva+24 Table 2 associates 150,000 K with Knigge+97, whose original quantity was not checked.
issues.why_it_matters: WD temperature comparisons can be biased if model inputs, heated patches, and UV disc/wind components are treated as photospheric measurements.
issues.needed_action: Retrieve/inspect Hartley+05 and Knigge+97 full original text and decide which WD photosphere solution, if any, merits a compact preferred field; retain all alternatives in ledger.

issues.competing_evidence: Thorstensen+03 raw pi_abs=8.9 +/-1.7 mas; parallax+proper-motion posterior 164(+88/-42) pc; body reports final 160(+65/-37) pc while Table 4 gives 163(+68/-38) pc after distance-modulus prior 6.2 +/-1.5 mag. Gaia DR3 pi=4.663355 +/-0.025915 mas; Bailer-Jones geometric posterior 213.497 pc [212.243,214.740]. Exact Gaia DR2 query gives 4.436867 +/-0.040324 mas; Harrison+18 prints 4.467 +/-0.05 mas and allows ~0.3 mas systematics. Gaia DR3 RUWE=1.7625 and excess-noise significance=91.0.
issues.why_it_matters: Distance changes affect luminosities and separate historical model assumptions from Gaia astrometry; the DR2 paper/archive mismatch and elevated DR3 excess noise may matter despite exact counterpart identity.
issues.needed_action: Confirm whether the Gaia EDR3 geometric posterior remains the catalog reference distance after review of Gaia astrometric systematics/variability; retain body/table distance reports and DR2 query/paper values separately; do not invert or average parallaxes.

issues.competing_evidence: Saitou+12 Table 1 reports 5.8(+1.1/-1.2)e8 cm from a mass-radius relation. Boneva+24 repeats 5.4e8 cm in prose, then Eq. (2)/Table 2 reports 3.11e8 cm and 0.004 +/-0.002 Rsun using M1=0.99 Msun; evaluating the printed equation with its stated inputs gives about 5.33e8 cm, not 3.11e8.
issues.why_it_matters: WD radius is a core physical comparison and the Boneva output is not reproducible from its stated formula/mass.
issues.needed_action: Check Boneva equation/typesetting or calculation with the authors/source model; until then use neither Boneva 3.11e8 cm nor its converted solar-radius entry as a preferred value.

issues.competing_evidence: Saitou+12 presents Suzaku spectral fits over 0.35-40 keV and hard 2-10 keV luminosity at assumed d=163 pc; Ridder+23 Table 4 values 4.7 +/-0.5e-12 (1-10 keV) and 5.7 +/-0.6e-12 (0.1-10 keV) are asterisked PIMMS/MEKAL conversions and unabsorbed estimates, using an approximately 11-keV characteristic temperature. Neither is simultaneous with 2014 VLA data.
issues.why_it_matters: Bandpass, absorption and assumed distance determine interpretation of flux/luminosity comparisons.
issues.needed_action: If a preferred X-ray comparison value is needed, choose native Suzaku model products or the approximate converted catalog bands explicitly; preserve epoch, model and absorption convention.

issues.competing_evidence: Coppejans+16 Sec. 2.1 summarizes old upper limits, including roughly <0.1 mJy at 4.885 GHz and limits 1.1/4.6 mJy at 5 GHz and 25 mJy at 10.6 GHz; exact paper-to-limit mapping and original confidence conventions were not fully reconstructed from Fuerst+86, Nelson & Spencer+88, and Woodsworth & Hughes+77.
issues.why_it_matters: Historical radio sensitivity comparisons can be wrong if a limit is assigned to the wrong epoch/frequency/source or confidence level.
issues.needed_action: Inspect the original three historical radio papers and map each limit to observation date, state, bandwidth, and confidence before including them in public-facing comparisons.
